messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: unexpected posterior predictive node
parts:
I have a vary complicated model, a part of which specifies a constrained (sex-specific) gam for some period effects (code for that part below). When I configureMCMC step and it assignes the samples, the precision parameter for females (tau_period_foi_female) is assigned a RW sampler, as expected, but the male parameter (tau_period_foi_male), which as far as I can tell is specified identically, is assigne a posterior predictive sampler. 

I don't understand why this should be the case, and I'd appreciate any suggestions.

Thanks,
Glenn

<relevant code>
  tau_period_foi_male ~ dgamma(1, 1) # this gets assigned a PP sampler
  tau_period_foi_female ~ dgamma(1, 1)
 
  for (k in 1:nknots_foi_cgam) {
  ln_b_foi_cgam_f[k] ~ dnorm(0, tau_period_foi_female)
  b_foi_cgam_f[k] <- exp(ln_b_foi_cgam_f[k])
 
  ln_b_foi_cgam_m[k] ~ dnorm(0, tau_period_foi_male)
  b_foi_cgam_m[k] <- exp(ln_b_foi_cgam_m[k])
  }
 
  for (t in 1:nT_period_foi) {
  f_period_foi_cgam_temp[t] <- inprod(b_foi_cgam_f[1:nknots_foi_cgam],
  Z_foi_cgam[t, 1:nknots_foi_cgam])
  f_period_foi_cgam[t] <- f_period_foi_cgam_temp[t] - f_mu_foi_cgam
 
  m_period_foi_cgam_temp[t] <- inprod(b_foi_cgam_m[1:nknots_foi_cgam],
  Z_foi_cgam[t, 1:nknots_foi_cgam])
  m_period_foi_cgam[t] <- m_period_foi_cgam_temp[t] - m_mu_foi_cgam
  }
 
  m_mu_foi_cgam <- mean(m_period_foi_cgam_temp[1:nT_period_foi])
  f_mu_foi_cgam <- mean(f_period_foi_cgam_temp[1:nT_period_foi])

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: unexpected posterior predictive node
parts:
Glenn, I'd be curious to look into this, but would need a reproducible example to see what's going on.

By virtue of being assigned a posterior_predictive sampler, it means that (at least as configureMCMC is able to determine) there are no data nodes downstream from (dependent upon) the "tau_period_foi_male" model parameter.  This could in fact be the case, and maybe that's a result of the model or the data.  Or, perhaps it's a bug with configureMCMC's analysis of the model.  But it's impossible to tell without being able to reproduce (and further investigate) what you're observing.

That said, a quick glance a the model code you sent doesn't immediate present any downstream data nodes.  The ln_b_foi_cgam_m[k] terms appear to be random effects, and at quick glance, I don't see any stochastic (thus, potentially data) dependencies of the ln_b_foi_cgam_m[k] nodes.

I hope this helps a little,
Daniel

messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: Re: unexpected posterior predictive node
parts:
Thanks Daniel! That was quick and very helpful response - your point about downstream data nodes was the spark I needed. 

The period effects feed into a custom nimble function further down the code, and I was inadvertently providing the female effect (the second time) instead of the male effect to that function. Fixed that and now it is behaving as expected. 

Glenn
